title: Review of membrane_evo L7[L3]: the high-yield allele wins on 3/3 fresh seeds against identical-event twins, but with p_death=0 the population freezes and neither division nor selection happens (Weak)
summary: Looked at the claim's up-arm sheet, then ran membrane_evo_up and its identical-event twin membrane_evo on fresh seeds 21, 22 and 23 (claim protocol, --frames 160 --spf 250, T=40000), plus both arms with the imposed death disk switched off (p_death=0, seeds 21 and 22). Final K2 biomass share, up vs twin: 0.93 vs 0.46, 0.78 vs 0.30, 0.82 vs 0.02 (share.txt), so the sign replicates. Trajectories are very noisy: on seed 22 the up arm lost K2 completely at frame 101 (share 0.40 -> 0.00) and regained it by fresh flips, and the twin reached 0.54 at frame 141. Up arms reach generation 3-4 with 5-11 persistent splits. Without disk deaths the population freezes by t~10000 at 6-13 cells: 0-1 persistent splits per run, cells sit still while flips recolour them, and the shares no longer separate (0.07 vs 0.32, 0.65 vs 0.50). So in this world both reproduction and selection are driven by the imposed disturbance, which supports the committee's 'disturbance-mediated' caveat and suggests that Q:autonomous-l7-identity-deaths must also supply turnover, not only replace the disk.

verdicts.limitation: Direction replicates but I did not extract per-kind births, deaths or conversions, and 11 cells on seed 23 carry both kinds (merges). The p_death=0 control shows the population freezes without the imposed disks: reproduction and selection are both disturbance-driven, so this is selection under imposed turnover, not autonomous L7.
